title: Bound on an Array Read
statement: Let $\mu:\mathbb{N}\to\mathbb{Z}$, let $a,N,\mathrm{top},i\in\mathbb{N}$, let $l$ be a list of integers, and let $U\in\mathbb{Z}$. Suppose $l$ has length $N$, its $j$th entry is $\mu(a+j)$ for every $j<N$, every entry $x$ of $l$ satisfies $|x|\le U$, and $a+N\le\mathrm{top}$. Then $|\mu(a+i)|\le U$ whenever $i<N$.
hypotheses_covered: The list records μ(a+j) at each index j<N
Every list entry has absolute value at most U
